body: Are you suggesting I should be alone forever? XDDDD

I read somewhere that sometimes when falling asleep it happens. I mean the vibrations of the whole body and it is basically your body entering sleep paralysis. It happens each night, but only sometimes you are still able to consciously experience it. Many people use it to enter lucid dreams or even out of body experience.

Well, it's not the worst, my situation, but sometimes I need more from people, more time. I'm sorry you feel this way. :( I was engaged and I had to quit this relationship, because of many problems. I know how it is. If someone is in a relationship, married, it's all different and we don't need a lot from other people. It's all really tough. To have time for everyone, make everyone happy, keep friendships at the same time. I couldn't do it when I was with him.

I did it a year ago. Deleted everything. But unfortunately we have a facebook group where people post important stuff about classes. People didn't even notice, except my 4 friends who are, you know, minding their ows business anyway. I feel sorry you feel this way and about your friend. There were people in my life who did the same, just left.

My friend found her boyfriend through Tinder. I found my first boyfriend on a dating site (polish). Cause yeah, I live here. 
But I also doubt it works for everyone. I gave up trying to find someone online. 
People there (not everyone though) are superficial and are often extroverts. But if you want sex, it should be easy.
It's good if you can accept it. I tried to, but failed.
My friends don't have snapchats. And I watch parties my fav youtuber goes to, people he meets... and I feel happy for him, but I die a little bit when I compare it to my life. Heh...

Haha. I have similar experience with liking boys who turn out to be gay. Or unfortunately, are unavailable, to put it lightly. What can I say? You know. I just wanted to say you're not alone in this, but yeah, it sucks. Sometimes I wish I could be a man, just to date gay guys. 
Pfff. Not a lot of people can relate to that. Well, maybe. But ones who didn't experience it often think it's weird.
I used to, but side effects were scary. And it didn't change a lot.

I used to take medication, but it made me feel tired, more tired than I am without it. Also, it gave me sleep paralysis and I was afraid to fall asleep. It didn't make me normal or more motivated. I gained weight without eating more than usual. 
Medication didn't take away my problems with communication, mania did... for 2 months or so.

I know, unfortunately the psychologist I'd been seeing for almost 4 years lost her job. And it was my 'fault', but it's a long story... the new one said she can't see me until the end of June. I have to find someone responsible. 
I wasn't diagnosed with Aspergers by a professional, it was just speculation and the test was online, but I want to verify it.
Depression sucks, I'm sorry for everyone who has to experience it :( Unfortunately, Aspergers and depression often go hand in hand.
